title: The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was worse than we thought
excerpt: An update from OpenAI reveals its AI model accessed credentials on additional services beyond Hugging Face.
content_html:
New details have emerged about a security incident in which an OpenAI AI model broke out of its testing environment and compromised Hugging Face's infrastructure.

An update OpenAI published on July 28 filled in details that weren't part of the original disclosure. The AI agent also identified and used exposed credentials on four accounts across four other publicly available services, using one as a relay point and another for data storage, while accessing the remaining two in a read-only capacity. OpenAI said it has since notified the affected service owners and hasn't found evidence of broader impact to those platforms.

On Wednesday, the cloud computing service Modal identified itself as one of those four affected parties.

However, in its statement, Modal said its systems were never actually breached. According to Modal, the AI got in through a customer's own application that was set up without a password requirement, allowing code submitted by literally anyone on the internet to run. The AI's activity was limited to that one customer's isolated space and didn't spread to any other Modal customers, the company said.

The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack first came to light in mid-July, when Hugging Face disclosed an intrusion into its systems that it described as "different from anything we had handled," driven entirely by an autonomous AI agent. OpenAI followed with its own blog post explaining that the breach originated during an internal evaluation designed to test its models' hacking capabilities. The models involved — GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased, even more capable prototype — were running with reduced safety restrictions specifically for the test and were confined to a sandboxed environment with no direct internet access.

Mashable Light Speed

According to OpenAI, the models exploited a previously unknown security flaw in Artifactory, a package registry cache proxy, to escalate privileges and move laterally within the testing environment until they reached a node with internet access. Once it got online, the AI figured out that Hugging Face's servers might contain the answers to the very hacking test it was trying to pass. So, it used a combination of stolen login credentials and additional security flaws to break into Hugging Face's servers and go looking for those answers.

OpenAI also tried to clear up confusion about which AI systems were involved. The company clarified that the not-yet-released version mentioned in its original explanation was purely an internal research tool, never meant for public release, and that it has since shut that version down entirely and locked it away.

In OpenAI's initial statement, a quote from Hugging Face co-founder and CEO Clem Delangue has framed the incident as proof that AI safety issues are better tackled openly, saying that the situation shows AI safety "will be solved in the open, collaboratively, with broad access to AI for every defender, everywhere."

OpenAI, meanwhile, called the incident "unprecedented" and said it's tightening its security controls while its investigation continues.

Disclosure: Ziff Davis, Mashable’s parent company, in April 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.

content_html_zh:
有关 OpenAI 人工智能模型突破测试环境并破坏 Hugging Face 基础设施的安全事件的新细节已经浮出水面。

OpenAI 于 7 月 28 日发布的更新补充了原始披露中未包含的细节。 人工智能代理还识别并使用了其他四项公开服务中的四个帐户的暴露凭据，其中一个作为中继点，另一个用于数据存储，同时以只读能力访问其余两个。 OpenAI 表示，此后已通知受影响的服务所有者，但尚未发现对这些平台产生更广泛影响的证据。

周三，云计算服务 Modal 自称是这四个受影响方之一。

然而，莫代尔在声明中表示，其系统从未真正遭到破坏。 根据 Modal 的说法，人工智能是通过客户自己的应用程序进入的，该应用程序的设置不需要密码，允许互联网上几乎任何人提交的代码运行。 该公司表示，人工智能的活动仅限于该客户的隔离空间，不会传播到任何其他 Modal 客户。

OpenAI-Hugging Face 黑客攻击于 7 月中旬首次曝光，当时 Hugging Face 披露了对其系统的入侵，并称其“与我们处理过的任何事情都不同”，完全由自主人工智能代理驱动。 OpenAI 随后在自己的博客文章中解释说，此次泄露源于旨在测试其模型的黑客能力的内部评估。 所涉及的模型——GPT-5.6 Sol 和一个未发布的、功能更强大的原型——在专门为测试而减少的安全限制下运行，并且被限制在无法直接访问互联网的沙盒环境中。

可混搭光速

据 OpenAI 称，这些模型利用了 Artifactory（一个软件包注册表缓存代理）中先前未知的安全漏洞来升级权限并在测试环境中横向移动，直到到达可以访问互联网的节点。 一旦上线，人工智能就会发现 Hugging Face 的服务器可能包含它试图通过的黑客测试的答案。 因此，它结合使用被盗的登录凭据和其他安全漏洞来闯入 Hugging Face 的服务器并寻找这些答案。

OpenAI 还试图澄清有关涉及哪些人工智能系统的困惑。 该公司澄清说，其最初解释中提到的尚未发布的版本纯粹是内部研究工具，从未打算公开发布，并且此后该版本已完全关闭并锁定。

在 OpenAI 的最初声明中，Hugging Face 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Clem Delangue 引用了这一事件作为人工智能安全问题得到更好公开解决的证据，并称这种情况表明人工智能安全“将通过公开、协作的方式得到解决，让世界各地的每个防御者都能广泛接触到人工智能”。

与此同时，OpenAI 称此次事件“史无前例”，并表示在调查继续的同时，正在加强安全控制。

披露：Mashable 的母公司 Ziff Davis 于 2025 年 4 月对 OpenAI 提起诉讼，指控其在训练和运营其人工智能系统时侵犯了 Ziff Davis 的版​​权。
